identity.title: Resolving the stellar activity of the Mira AB binary with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: based on ALMA science verification observations in Band 3 ($\sim94.6$ GHz) and Band 6 ($\sim228.7$ GHz), from the binary Mira A (${\rm o}$ Ceti) and Mira B.

evidence.quote: Mira is the closest symbiotic binary star (at 92 pc, (cite: vanLeeuwen07))

question.value: What are the size, shape, flux densities and spectral indices of Mira A and Mira B at mm wavelengths, and what do they imply about the extended atmosphere, stellar activity and the wind around Mira B?

evidence.quote: We present the size, shape and flux densities at millimeter continuum wavelengths, based on ALMA science verification observations
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00014.SV

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Band 3: three 2 GHz continuum SPWs (128 channels) at 89.176, 91.234, 99.192 GHz; Band 6: one 2 GHz SPW centered at 228.558 GHz

evidence.quote: In Band 3, three continuum spectral windows were observed with 128 channels over 2 GHz bandwidth centered on 89.176 GHz, 91.234 GHz and 99.192 GHz.

angular_resolution.value: Band 3: 72x64 mas and 68x57 mas; Band 6: 34x24 mas

evidence.quote: This resulted in a beam of $72\times64$ mas and a position angle of $78.8^\circ$ on October 17
The rms sensitivity was $\sim40~\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ in both epochs of the Band 3 and $\sim130~\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ in both epochs of the Band 6 observations.
Mira was observed on 17 and 25 October 2014 (Band 3) and 29 October and 1 November 2014 (Band 6).

findings_qualitative.value: Mira A disc is elongated and larger at Band 6 than Band 3, implying opacity changes and possible non-radial pulsations

evidence.quote: The elongation and wavelength dependent size of Mira A point to strong changes of opacity source throughout the extended envelope and possible non-radial pulsations.

claims.hypothesis: Is the Mira B emission from an ionized cavity or from Mira B's wind?
claims.experiment: uv-fit sizes and spectral index of Mira B compared with ionized cavity and wind expectations
claims.result: Size ~2.4 AU, alpha=1.3±0.2 with no turnover to 89 GHz
claims.finding: Emission from partially ionized gravitationally bound material from Mira A's wind, density at least an order of magnitude higher than the wind

evidence.quote: The partially ionized region of $\sim2.4$ AU around Mira B requires a density at least an order of magnitude higher than expected from the Mira A wind.

claims.hypothesis: Does Mira A's atmosphere match radio photosphere model predictions?
claims.experiment: Measured spectral indices and Tb compared to Reid & Menten model
claims.result: Tb at 3 mm ~5300 K, alpha shallower between bands
claims.finding: Tb in Band 3 significantly higher than predicted, possibly shock heating

evidence.quote: The brightness temperature at 3 mm is significantly higher than predicted in the radio photosphere model from (cite: reidment97).

claims.hypothesis: Is there a hotspot on Mira A's disc?
claims.experiment: Residual analysis and added Gaussian component in Band 6 uv-fits
claims.result: Compact component ~10 mJy, ~4.7 mas, Tb ~10000 K
claims.finding: Hotspot likely due to magnetic activity, possibly related to X-ray outburst

evidence.quote: though cannot rule out a cluster of delta functions.

why_this_method.value: Analysis done on uv-data to avoid deconvolution artifacts

evidence.quote: Most of the data analysis was performed directly on the $uv$-data in order to avoid image deconvolution artifacts

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Mira B wind contribution ruled out as too faint by 4 orders of magnitude

evidence.quote: We therefore rule out any significant contribution from Mira B’s wind at ALMA frequencies.

limitations_admitted.value: Band 3 resolution too poor to confirm the hotspot there; 25 Oct Band 3 epoch affected by resolved calibrator

evidence.quote: the worse angular resolution did not allow us to confidently distinguish between a fit of a stellar disc plus compact component or a stellar disc alone.

referee_caveats_inferred: Hotspot interpretation depends on model choice (Gaussian vs cluster of points) and single-band detection
Self-calibration on the strong source could bias small-scale structure
Absolute calibration depends on variable quasars; Band 6 epoch uses a different calibrator spectral index
